Chief Metropolitan Magistrate - Ii (New Delhi), Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Cc No. 173/10 Unique Case Id No. 02403R0323152010 Date of Institution: 10.12.2010 Date of reserving judgement: 16.12.2016 Date of pronouncement: 10.01.2017 In re: Delhi Administration / Food Inspector Department of Pfa, Govt. of Nct of Delhi A-20, Lawrence Road Industrial Area, Delhi-110035 ... texts.facts: The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (Pfa Act), wherein it is alleged that the accused had sold misbranded food in violation of Section 2 (ix)(k) of PFA Act read with Rule 32 and 42(zzz)(17) of PFA Rules, as punishable under Section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act. 2. As per the complaint, on 26.07.2010, the food officials including Food Inspector (FI) Ashok Kumar Singh and Field Assistant (FA) J. S. Bisht under the supervision of Local Health Authority (LHA)/SDM Sh. R. K. Sharma reached at the premises of M/s. Ram Narayan Prem Narayan at 403A, Khari Baoli, Delhi-110006, where the accused in the capacity of its vendor-cum-proprietor was found conducting the business of various food articles, including 'Kala Namak', which was found stored for sale for human consumption, lying in sealed packets of 500 gms. each bearing no label declaration. The food officials lifted the sample the said food article consisting of 03 such sealed packets of Kala Namak ready for sale. It was divided into three parts as per procedure prescribed under the PFA Act and Rules and separately packed and sealed. Necessary documents were prepared at the spot including the vendor's receipt and panchanama. Price of the sample was paid to the vendor. One counterpart of the sample was deposited with the Public Analyst (PA) and remaining two counterparts were deposited with SDM/LHA. Vide report dated 20.08.2010, the PA reported that the article was conforming to the standards, yet the sample was found misbranded being in complete violation of Rule 32 and 42(zzz) (17) of PFA Rules, because there was no label or In Re vs Sh. Ashok Kumar Gupta on 10 January, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92921259/ 1 the "vegetarian symbol". Based on the report of PA, investigation was carried out by the Food Inspector as per the instructions of the SDM/LHA. After completion of investigation and after obtaining due sanction of the Director, PFA, the present complaint was filed against the accused for violation of the section 2(ix)(k) read with Rule 32 and 42(zzz)(17), as punishable under Section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act for selling misbranded food. 3. Since the complaint was filed by a public servant in writing, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 28.01.2011. Based on the report of PA, notice of accusation under section 251 CrPC was framed vide order dated 08.08.2011 against the accused for commission of offence under Section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 4. At the trial, the prosecution examined three witnesses in support of its case. PW-1 Sh. R. K. Sharma (SDM/LHA), PW-2 FI A. K. Singh and PW-3 FA J. S. Bisht were the part of the team that had visited the premises of accused and lifted the sample of Kala Namak lying in sealed packets of 500 gms each. These witnesses deposed about the sample proceedings conducted by them on 26.07.2010 and narrated the steps undertaken by them, including disclosing their identity, lifting of 03 sealed packets of 500 gms each, dividing the same in three counterparts by putting 1 sealed packet as one counterpart and separately packing them. A sum of Rs. 30/- was paid to the vendor as price of the sample vide vendor's receipt Ex. PW-1/A. Notice in Form-VI Ex. PW-1/B, Panchnama Ex. PW-1/C and Raid Report Ex. PW-1 /D. One counterpart was deposited with the PA vide receipt Ex. PW-2/A and remaining two counterparts were deposited with SDM/LHA vide receipt Ex. PW-1/E. PA report Ex. PW-1/F was received opining the sample to be misbranded. Further investigation was carried out during which letter Ex. PW-2/B was sent to the accused vendor which was replied vide Ex. PW-2/B-1. In the meanwhile, representation of the accused Ex. PW-2/B-2 and their copies Ex PW-2/B-3 and Ex. PW2/B- 4 were received by the FI PW-2. Letter Ex. PW2/C and Ex. PW-2/C-1 were sent to VATO and DHO respectively which were never replied. After completion of investigation, consent for prosecution Ex. PW-1/G was taken from the Director, PFA, after which the complaint Ex. PW-1/H was filed and intimation letter Ex. PW-1/I was sent to the accused vide postal receipt Ex. PW-2/D. These witnesses were duly cross examined by the Ld. Defence Counsel for the accused, wherein they denied that there was no misbranding or that the sample procedure was not proper or that accused was forced to make endorsement on the documents. 5. Statement of the accused was recorded under section 313 CrPC on 17.03.2015 wherein he denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. Accused accepted the proceedings dated 26.07.2010 but claimed that the commodity was not for sale at that time and that it was packed because it was rainy day. He claimed that the sample was taken without his consent, that no efforts were made by the FI to join public witnesses, that no price was paid to him, that the FI did not adopt correct sample proceedings, that the documents were not read over and explained to him and that the food article was not for sale. No defence evidence was however led by them.
texts.arguments: 6. It is in these circumstances, Ld. SPP for the complainant has argued that the complainant has been able to prove its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt, as all the witnesses have supported its case and there is no condition in their testimony. It is submitted that the accused has In Re vs Sh. Ashok Kumar Gupta on 10 January, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92921259/ 2 failed to rebut the findings as given by the PA. 7. On the other hand, Ld. Defence Counsel for the accused has submitted that the prosecution case fails on technical grounds. Ld. Counsel submits that accused was not selling the food article and had only packed the same to prevent it from contamination due to rainy season. It is submitted that the sample method was not proper as the FI was required to open the packets, transfer its contents to a different container, then to mix the same properly and thereafter pack and seal them separately. . . Section 2. Definitions- (ix) 'misbranded'- an article of food shall be deemed to be misbranded- (k) if it is not labelled in accordance with the requirements of this Act or rules made thereunder; (x) "package" means a box, bottle, casket, tin, barrel, case, receptacle, sack, bag, wrapper or other thing other which an article of food is placed or packed. (f) Date of manufacture or packing.- The date, month and year in which the commodity is manufactured, packed or pre- packed shall be given on the label: ... The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Shriram Labhaya v. MCD [1948-1997 FAC (SC) 483] has categorically held that testimony of the Food Inspector alone, if believed, is sufficient to convict the accused and there is no requirement of independent corroboration by public persons unless the testimony suffers from fatal inconsistencies.
